source: Minchat Shai on Gen 9:29 (his longest Genesis note — the two camps)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION, the block's headline — ויהיו כל ימי נח ("and all the days of Noah WERE," plural): the manuscript war Minchat Shai documents at length. One camp (the Jericho chumash, old manuscripts, the Ramah's seven-count Masorah): Enoch and Lamech singular, NOAH PLURAL. The other (the Hilleli, all Sepharad books, the Ezra codex, Or Torah, Minchat Kohen, the Ramah's own scroll per the Burgos sages): Noah SINGULAR, a three-member list. SNAPSHOT reads PLURAL — the Jericho camp — and its own ledger census agrees end to end: seven plural totals in the ledger plus Noah, with EXACTLY Enoch and Lamech singular — the two-singular anomaly gen_14's derivation held unexplained is the Jericho tradition's own sign (their mnemonic: the two, "until Elijah comes"). Both camps recorded; the letter locked.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 36:8; Megillah 9b:4; Mishnah Megillah 1:8; Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:2
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION CHARTER - THE VERSE THAT LICENSES THIS CORPUS'S OWN SECOND TRACK. Our 9:27, 'may God expand Yefet, and he shall dwell in the TENTS OF SHEM', is read by Bar Kappara as meaning that the Torah's words may be SAID IN GREEK inside Shem's tents, and R. Yudan states it outright: 'from here, a source from the Torah for TRANSLATIONS'. The reading is then law: the case-table records the dispute over which languages a scroll may be written in, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's ruling permitting Greek alone is ruled as binding - with THIS VERSE given as the reason. A permission to render Scripture in another tongue is derived from a blessing about tents.

check.note: The verse from which the tradition derives its own license to translate Scripture - the ground of the Aramaic track this corpus reads beside the Hebrew.

middah: plain (the tents-of-Shem clause read as the license for translations — Megillah 9b)

claim_en: THE DRUNKENNESS VERSE CARRIES AN INK POINT AND A COUNT DISPUTE. Our 9:21 writes אָהֳלֹה ('his tent') with a final HEH rather than the expected vav - verified in the ink at derivation - and the chain reads the feminine suffix as HER tent, turning the exposure into an offence against his wife's quarters. The reflexive uncovering-verb is read as bringing EXILE upon himself and his descendants. And the number of woe-marking particles in the wine passage is itself disputed between seats, one counting fourteen and another thirteen - a numeric variance carried dual-track rather than resolved.

check.note: A pronominal suffix written unexpectedly, verified in the ink at derivation; plus a woe-particle count that two seats give differently, both carried per credit guard 3.

middah: ink (his-tent with the final heh; the reading and the count dispute beside)

claim_en: WHAT WAS ACTUALLY DONE TO HIM IS DISPUTED, AND THE DISPUTE DECIDES WHY THE CURSE FALLS WHERE IT DOES. Rav and Shmuel divide: one holds he was castrated, the other that he was sodomized - the castration reading argued from the missing fourth son, the other by verbal analogy on the seeing-verb. The resolution offered is that all agree on castration and some add the second. And the question the machine cannot answer from the text - why the curse lands on Canaan rather than on the offender - is answered two ways: because a curse cannot land where the blessing of 9:1 already stands, or because Canaan saw and told.

check.note: The offence itself disputed between two mechanisms, with the misplaced target of the curse explained two ways.

middah: plain (the recorded dispute over the act; the seeing-verb's verbal analogy, E7, on one arm)

source: Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:3:1; Bereshit Rabbah 61:7; Bereshit Rabbah 60:7
claim_en: THE CURSE OF OUR 9:25 FOSSILIZES INTO LEGAL VOCABULARY AND IS PLEADED IN A REAL TRIBUNAL - YET IT IS EXITABLE. Every Gentile slave in the case-tables is called a 'CANAANITE slave' after this verse's 'slave of slaves', the curse becoming the standing category name of a whole body of law. Before Alexander it is pleaded as property law - a slave's acquisitions belong to his master - to defeat a territorial claim. And against all of that the chain records the status as escapable: Canaan and Eliezer are identified as one, and service of the righteous moved him from cursed to blessed, 'Come, blessed of the Lord'.

check.note: A curse that becomes a legal category name and a courtroom pleading, and is simultaneously recorded as an exitable status.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: LIVE PRAYER LAW RESTS ON THE FACT THAT THIS SUBJECT IS NOT AN ISRAELITE. Rav Yehuda rules that a gentile's nakedness counts as nakedness for the purpose of reciting the Shema, and his proof is our 9:23 - 'their father's nakedness' said of a man who was not an Israelite. The verse's own subject is the argument.

check.note: A ruling that depends specifically on the non-Israelite status of this unit's subject.

middah: plain (the verse's own non-Israelite subject as the proof — Berakhot 25b)

claim_en: TWO FURTHER LAWS AND A HISTORICAL VERDICT RIDE THIS SPAN. From 'he SAW... and he TOLD' the organs of the offence are identified as the eye and the tooth, which the chain roots to the later law freeing a slave maimed in eye or tooth. And R. Yochanan decides a question of Temple history from our 9:27: the Divine Presence did not rest in the second Temple, because Yefet's sponsorship could ENLARGE the house but the dwelling belongs to Shem alone.

check.note: An offence's organs read as the root of a later manumission law, and a Temple-history verdict decided from this verse's own division of roles.
